newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PAL says aircraft purchases to go ahead.
newsitem.headline: PAL says aircraft purchases to go ahead.

text.p: Philippine Airlines Inc (PAL) will press ahead with an ambitious $4 billion refleeting and modernisation programme following the settlement of a wage dispute with its pilots, an airline official said on Thursday.

"With the agreement with the pilots, we have contacted the different aircraft manufacturers and we will proceed with the order that we've had," Manolo Aquino, airline executive vice president, told Reuters.
"Training ( of the pilots) will commence," he said, adding that this was put on hold while the management and a 615-member pilots union wrangled over salaries and conditions of work.
The two sides came to an agreement on Tuesday but have not revealed details.
The refleeting programme involves 36 aircraft, including eight 747-400s from Boeing Co and 28 aircraft from Airbus Industrie, including A340-200s, A340-300s, A320-300s and A330-300s.
Newspapers have said the purchases could have been cut in half if the wage negotiations had broken down.
